projects.name: Personal Conversation RAG
projects.shortDescription: Local-first semantic search across ChatGPT conversation exports and personal notes, with local embeddings and storage.
projects.description: A modular Python retrieval system built on ports-and-adapters architecture. Imports ChatGPT exports and markdown notes, streams JSON shards directly from ZIP archives, generates local embeddings via Ollama, and queries ChromaDB. Claude imports and grounded answer generation are planned for later phases.
projects.impact: Brings conversation exports and personal notes into a searchable local index without requiring paid cloud APIs for retrieval.
highlights: Local-first architecture using local BGE-M3 multilingual embeddings via Ollama
Memory-efficient streaming of large export archives and JSON shards (ijson)
Conversation graph-aware chunking preserving branching turns with deterministic deduplication
Clean ports-and-adapters architecture with strict type safety (Mypy strict, Pydantic v2)

cover.alt: RAG interface preview with a search field and filters for ChatGPT conversations and notes.

caseStudy.summary: The retrieval foundation of a personal RAG system: semantic search over ChatGPT exports and markdown notes using local Ollama embeddings and ChromaDB. Answer generation is a later phase.
caseStudy.problem: Finding a past decision across conversation exports and notes takes manual searching. Large exports also contain nested message graphs and multiple JSON shards, making whole-file parsing expensive in memory.
caseStudy.solution: Built a Python pipeline using ijson to stream ZIP archives shard-by-shard, with conversation-aware chunking and stable identifiers. Local BGE-M3 embeddings via Ollama and Dockerized ChromaDB provide the retrieval layer.
caseStudy.outcome: The CLI supports ingestion, indexing, and search with source metadata and distance. The ChatGPT importer has been checked against a real account export. Full-corpus indexing and the final search smoke test remain to be validated. Quality checks include strict Mypy, Ruff, and an 85% branch-coverage gate.
lessons: Processing gigabyte-scale chat exports requires streaming (ijson) and tree graph traversal rather than naive whole-file in-memory parsing.
Decoupling domain logic from provider formats (ports-and-adapters) enables adding new importers without altering the indexing pipeline.
Bridging native host Ollama with Docker Compose application services maximizes GPU acceleration while keeping runtime environments clean and reproducible.

sections.title: Architecture & Code Quality
sections.body: Ports-and-adapters architecture separates source importers, domain logic, and infrastructure. Pydantic v2 validates models, Typer provides the CLI, and the project configures strict Mypy, Ruff, and automated tests.

sections.title: Performance & Memory Efficiency
sections.body: Streaming from ZIP archives avoids loading the entire export into memory. Stable identifiers and SHA-256 hashes let repeated ingestion and indexing skip unchanged data. End-to-end runtime and memory measurements are still to be recorded.

projects.name: Starbounder
projects.shortDescription: A 2D space sandbox prototype: explore procedural star systems, land on planets, mine resources, and build colonies.
projects.description: Starbounder is a Unity/C# graduation project combining space exploration with sandbox and strategy mechanics. It extends an earlier procedural world generator into a gameplay loop of flying, landing, mining, building, and saving progress. Presented as a functional prototype, it provides a foundation for further development rather than a finished commercial game.
projects.role: Game design / Unity and C# development
projects.impact: Turned an earlier procedural generator into a playable prototype connecting exploration, resource gathering, colony construction, UI, and saved progress.
highlights: Seed-based star systems with procedural planet meshes, biomes, textures, and resources
Parallel biome, texture, and spawn calculations using Job System and Burst
Ship flight, planetary gravity zones, landing, and on-foot exploration
Mining, shared inventory, and data-driven colony buildings with costs and dependencies
Galaxy Hub, compass, sector map, inventory, and building panels built with UI Toolkit
Per-galaxy JSON saves for the ship, inventory, buildings, and extractor state

cover.alt: A procedurally generated green planet in Starbounder against stars and nebulae

caseStudy.summary: A graduation prototype that turns procedural space generation into an interconnected sandbox experience. The work focused on integrating gameplay systems and improving world-generation performance.
caseStudy.motivation: I started Starbounder to challenge myself with a more complex project and learn new technologies. I was particularly interested in procedural generation with Perlin noise and working with parallel and asynchronous systems in Unity.
caseStudy.problem: The previous school-year project could generate star systems and planets, but lacked the connected gameplay needed to make them worth exploring. The graduation assignment added ship physics, mining, colony construction, orbiting planets, and persistent progress.
caseStudy.solution: Seed-based generation creates the star system and planet surfaces. Burst-compiled parallel jobs compute biome maps, texture pixels, and spawn candidates. A player state machine switches between ship and on-foot controls, while ScriptableObject data drives resources and buildings. UI Toolkit exposes these systems through a Galaxy Hub, HUD, map, inventory, and construction panels.
caseStudy.outcome: Presented as a functional 2D space-game prototype with exploration, mining, colony construction, and per-galaxy saves. The final thesis reports a reduction in world initialization from roughly 30 seconds to 5 seconds after the Jobs/Burst refactor. The project remains a prototype with onboarding, economy balancing, and settings still to develop.
lessons: Moving generation into parallel jobs required restructuring data flow and explicitly synchronizing work before creating Unity objects.
ScriptableObject data separates resource and building parameters from gameplay code, making tuning and content expansion easier.
Regenerating the world from a seed before restoring saved progress simplifies persistence, but changed world objects still need explicit save data.
A working collection of systems needs onboarding and clear player goals to become an understandable game.

sections.title: Gameplay loop
sections.body: Create or select a galaxy, travel through its generated star system, land, and explore a planet on foot. Mine resources into a shared inventory, place buildings with costs and dependencies, and return to the hub with saved progress.

sections.title: World generation and performance
sections.body: The generator builds planet meshes and distributes biomes, resources, and decorations from seeds. Job System and Burst handle biome maps, texture pixels, and candidate spawn positions in parallel; coroutines spread initialization across frames. The reviewed project uses Unity 6000.2.8f1 and URP.

sections.title: Saving and restoring a galaxy
sections.body: JSON files store galaxy metadata and gameplay state separately. Loading first regenerates the star system, then restores ship position and energy, inventory, buildings, and extractor state. The player returns to the ship on load to avoid problems when resuming planetary physics.

sections.title: Prototype scope and next steps
sections.body: Testing during development was manual and scenario-based, with feedback from other players. Moon support and ship status indicators remain experimental, and the settings tab is unfinished. The next priorities are a guided first-session quest, economy balancing, settings and key rebinding, and more complete persistence of mined deposits. A WebGL portfolio embed remains a possible later step.
